dedupe_keys.name: estimated peak geoelectric field strengths during a carrington class magnetic storm usgs

description: This data set gives modelled estimates of peak one-minute geoelectric field strengths at 1,616 magnetotelluric survey sites across the contiguous United States during a hypothetical Carrington-class magnetic storm. It was published by the US Geological Survey with Jeffrey J. Love, Greg M. Lucas, Anna Kelbert, E. Joshua Rigler, Paul A. Bedrosian and Neesha R. Schnepf. Values are derived from magnetometer time series and magnetotelluric impedance tensors, and each site has a most likely value and a 68% confidence interval. Coverage is the 1,616 survey sites in the contiguous US. The data are downloadable from USGS ScienceBase (2025) under CC0 at no cost and are cited by a USGS Open-File Report and a related data release. Caveats: the storm is hypothetical, sites cover only surveyed areas, and field strengths must be combined with grid models to estimate currents in power lines. Simulation uses are geomagnetic storm hazard maps and screening of transmission networks for geomagnetically induced currents. Related records: data-great-britain-grid-gic-open-data covers GIC modelling in Great Britain.
